questions.question: What is the natural greenhouse effect?
options: Gases trapping heat to keep Earth warm enough for life
The destruction of the ozone layer
questions.explanation: The greenhouse effect is a natural process where gases trap heat, keeping Earth warm enough to sustain life.

questions.question: What did the Paris Agreement (2015) commit countries to?
options: Keeping warming well below 2°C, ideally 1.5°C, above pre-industrial levels
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement committed nations to keeping warming well below 2°C, with efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.

questions.question: What is the primary human cause of the enhanced greenhouse effect?
questions.explanation: Human activities, primarily burning fossil fuels and deforestation, have amplified the greenhouse effect.

questions.question: What is a climate "tipping point"?
options: A threshold beyond which changes become self-reinforcing and potentially irreversible
A point where all warming stops
questions.explanation: Climate tipping points are thresholds beyond which changes become self-reinforcing and potentially irreversible.

questions.question: Roughly what level of warming is the world currently on track for by 2100?
questions.explanation: Despite the Paris Agreement, the world is on track for roughly 2.7°C of warming by the end of the century.
